knowledge_point.title: Identifying Points That Lie on a Line

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186054676/assets/359b3493e092dd7f92b953f72c73cf94ebf32e99c09c8d8fb2a4629e726aae34.png)

Which of the given points lie on the line $y=-5x-2?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The plotted points correspond to the $xy$-pairs $A(-2,9),B(-1,4)$ and $C(1,-7).$

To check whether a point lies on the line, we substitute the coordinates of the point into the equation and determine whether the resulting statement is true.

- Substituting the point $A(-2,9)$ results in a false statement:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-5x-2 \\ (9) & =-5(-2)-2 \\ 9 & =8\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point $A$ does *not* lie on the line.

- Substituting the point $B(-1,4)$ results in a false statement:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-5x-2 \\ (4) & =-5(-1)-2 \\ 4 & =3\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point $B$ does not lie on the line.

- Substituting the point $C(1,-7)$ results in a true statement:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-5x-2 \\ (-7) & =-5(1)-2 \\ -7 & =-7\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point $C$ does lie on the line.

Finally, only point $C$ lies on the line.
